change: No changes. Primary (abs) and secondary (obliques, lats, anterior deltoids, lower back/erector spinae) confirmed correct. The band tension requires lats and anterior deltoids to stabilize the arms while the core works anti-extension and anti-rotation. Lower back (erector spinae) is a legitimate stabilizer in supine anti-extension work.

No changes. In the reverse rollout (feet on wheel, hands on floor, pike upward), primary is abs (upper and lower rectus) as the prime mover driving the pike. Secondary: obliques (anti-rotation stabilizers), anterior deltoids and lats (arm/shoulder bracing), quads/rectus femoris (hip flexion component of the pike). Data confirmed correct.

Added Abductor->Abductor as a 5th primary muscle group. Hip flexors (iliopsoas/rectus femoris) are well-documented prime movers in running, driving the swing leg forward. The Abductor bucket is the only valid mapping for hip flexion in this system. The existing four primary groups (Quads, Hamstrings, Calves, glutes) and three secondary groups (abs, Lower Back, Shin/Tibialis) were all confirmed correct and retained.

Two corrections: (1) Removed Gluteus Maximus from secondary. The hip abductor machine does not meaningfully engage Gluteus Maximus; it isolates Gluteus Medius and Gluteus Minimus (Minimus has no allowed mapping so omitted). Research confirms glute max activation is minimal on this machine. (2) Added Abductor->Abductor as secondary to represent Tensor Fasciae Latae (TFL), which is a confirmed secondary synergist in hip abduction per EMG literature. (3) Fixed rule violation: the original data had two separate 'glutes' bucket entries (primary: Gluteus Medius; secondary: Gluteus Maximus), which violates the merge-same-bucket rule. Since Gluteus Maximus is not warranted here, it is simply removed rather than merged.

No changes. Primary: all three quad heads confirmed correct (leg extension is a quad isolation). Secondary: obliques (External + Internal) retained per unilateral rule in CLAUDE.md — single-leg machine work does require trunk anti-rotation stabilization. Data confirmed correct.
